html:
The Aymara are an Indigenous people of the high Andes around Lake Titicaca, in Bolivia, southern Peru and northern Chile, numbering about two million. After the fall of Tiwanaku around 1000, the altiplano was divided among Aymara-speaking kingdoms such as the Colla, Lupaca and Pacajes, the Aymara kingdoms. They herded llamas and alpacas and farmed potatoes and quinoa at heights near 4,000 metres.

The Inca conquered them in the 1400s. Under Spain many were drafted for forced labour at the silver mines of Potosí, the source of Potosí silver. In 1781 the Aymara leader Túpac Katari besieged La Paz for months before he was captured and executed.

In 2006 Evo Morales, an Aymara, became Bolivia's first Indigenous president, and Bolivia renamed itself a plurinational state. The Aymara flag, the checkered wiphala, became an official symbol.
